description:
**#12953 Add Default Tests for Root and Homepage Pages in Wagtail Starter Projects** 
Added tests.py file in wagtail/wagtail/project_template/home/ with given code
Reinstalled wagtail locally through "pip install -e ."
Ran given tests "python manage.py test home" in created project directory.
Updated wagtail/docs/getting_started/tutorial.md

comments.body:
```suggestion
When you create a new project using `wagtail start`, there will be a set of basic tests included in the `home/tests.py` file.

These tests check:
```

Just a reword, we do not need to say 'now includes' as these docs will be read when the updates already exist. Also, we try to avoid repeating 'Wagtail' as it's the docs you are already looking at.

Just a refinement, avoiding bold and using the model as a code formatted proper noun.

```suggestion
-   If the _root `Page`_ (ID=1) is automatically created.
-   If the _home `Page`_ is created as a child of the root page.
-   If a `BlogIndexPage` (or other page types) can be added.
```

Also, adding extra spaces to the list, while we do not use Prettier in MD docs, it's going to get these extra spaces when we do manual clean up sometimes.

```suggestion

To run the tests, navigate to your project folder and run:
```

````suggestion
python manage.py test home
```
````

Missed the closing backticks.

Line break needed at the end of the file, minor formatting but it just means the CI will not complain.
Best to run your code formatter for new PRs.

See https://docs.wagtail.org/en/stable/contributing/python_guidelines.html#pep8

```suggestion
```

Do we need this comment? it does not look like we do this in any other template files.

I think we should try to use our documented testing approach in https://docs.wagtail.org/en/stable/advanced_topics/testing.html


```suggestion
from wagtail.test.utils import WagtailPageTestCase
```

Also, have a review of that page for some other tips/practice we recommend in our docs.

What is this actually testing?

Do we need some assertions here?

Same for the test above.

As a general point - we need to think very carefully about any changes to the tutorial, particularly ones so early in the steps, as this will often be the first impression that new users receive of Wagtail.

* We want to ensure that users following the tutorial see tangible results as quickly as possible. It's good to get users into the mindset of testing early, but do we really want to take them on a tangent before they've even seen the admin interface?
* The description of what these tests are checking includes concepts that haven't been explained yet - such as `BlogIndexPage` (is this actually true any more?) and, particularly, the idea that "root" is a page in its own right - I'd actually consider this to be an internal implementation detail that new users shouldn't have to know, and we'd generally avoid mentioning it directly, through wording like "create a page at the root level" rather than "create a page as a child of the root page".
* Have we checked that these tests continue to work correctly after we've extended HomePage?

Thanks @gasman 

Actually, I think there's a bit of confusion here. The code is adding starting tests to the temple, not to to the tutorial. 

I think this content is mean to go on https://docs.wagtail.org/en/stable/reference/project_template.html#project-templates-reference

Probably under the Django settings section, before the Docker file one.

Note, AI suggestion, but maybe we should do something else here to actually have a basic starting set of tests.

```suggestion
    def test_homepage_status_code(self):
        response = self.client.get(reverse('home'))
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)

    def test_homepage_template_used(self):
        response = self.client.get(reverse('home'))
        self.assertTemplateUsed(response, 'home/index.html')
```

Be sure to run this code yourself, ensuring the tests run for a new project.

I think we should choose to start with a set of tests that pass. It's possible it could cause confusion if the tutorial starting point does not pass.

I would recommend we actually remove this 'placeholder' test and just add a few more starting tests.
